name: Ethyl senecioate

papers.title: A new insecticidal protolimonoid from Aegle marmelos

research.basis: MeSH indexing and publication types of the most relevant PubMed records; counts are of papers in the sample, not findings.

vocabulary.structure: SEPIO assertion / evidence line / evidence item

evidence: Measured in 3 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.1–0.14% of total volatiles (0.02–0.028mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Ethyl senecioate is a natural ester, a family of compounds that typically give fruits and flowers their distinctive aromas. People most likely encounter this molecule in their daily lives when eating fresh, wild berries.
consumer_summary.found_in: This compound has been identified in Vaccinium angustifolium, commonly known as the wild lowbush blueberry.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to ethyl senecioate for its potential role in natural pest control. Early bench and animal research (Oxford level 5) is exploring whether compounds like this can act as effective insect repellents or insecticides. If this bears out, it could offer new, plant-derived ways to manage agricultural pests or household insects without relying on synthetic chemicals.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward ethyl senecioate having properties that may support natural insect deterrence.
structure_function.basis: This rests on a single animal-model study evaluating its insecticidal potential.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether ethyl senecioate can effectively repel or eliminate pests like houseflies and beetles, which could eventually lead to new botanical insecticides or personal repellents.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A controlled human volunteer study (arm-in-cage test) applying a topical dilution of ethyl senecioate to measure the time until first insect landing compared to a standard repellent like DEET over a 6-hour period.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is bench and animal research (Oxford level 5) focusing on its effects against insects.
